dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:9601.text: To descend from a height. Formed from 𨸏, with 員 indicating the sound. The Changes says: 'Something falls from heaven.'

shuowen:9602.text: Dangerous. Formed from 𨸏 and abbreviated 毀. Xu Xun takes 隉 as ominous; Attendant Jia says a rule or standard; Ban Gu says unsettled. The Book of Zhou says: 'The state's instability.' Read like 蜺 in 虹蜺.

shuowen:9603.text: A small collapse. Formed from 𨸏, with 也 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9604.text: A collapsed city wall or mound is called 隓. Formed from 𨸏, with 𢀡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9605.text: Slanting. Formed from 𨸏 and 頃; 頃 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:9606.text: To fall. Formed from 𨸏, with 多 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9607.text: A gate, according to the recorded 門 gloss. Formed from 𨸏, with 亢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9608.text: An open drainage channel. Formed from 𨸏, with 賣 indicating the sound. Read like 瀆.

shuowen:9609.text: An embankment. Formed from 𨸏, with 方 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9610.text: An embankment, 唐. Formed from 𨸏, with 是 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9611.text: A foundation. Formed from 𨸏, with 止 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9612.text: A break or depression across a mountain. Formed from 𨸏, with 坙 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9613.text: 附𡝤, a small earthen hill. Formed from 𨸏, with 付 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'Small earthen hills have no pines or cypresses.'

shuowen:9614.text: In Qin, hills and slopes are called 阺. Formed from 𨸏, with 氐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9615.text: A rocky mountain capped with earth. Formed from 𨸏 and 兀; 兀 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:9616.text: A cliff. Formed from 𨸏, with 兼 indicating the sound. Read like 儼.

shuowen:9617.text: To block. Formed from 𨸏, with 戹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9618.text: To obstruct. Formed from 𨸏, with 鬲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9619.text: To separate or obstruct. Formed from 𨸏, with 章 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9620.text: To conceal. Formed from 𨸏, with 㥯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9621.text: A bend in water; a bank. Formed from 𨸏, with 奧 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9622.text: A bend in water; a recess. Formed from 𨸏, with 畏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9623.text: 𦥳商, a small clod. Formed from 𨸏 and 臾.

shuowen:9624.text: A Water Administration official; also, a valley, as the source's compressed wording records. Formed from 𨸏, with 解 indicating the sound. Alternatively, a small stream.

shuowen:9625.text: The great slope in 天水. Formed from 𨸏, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9626.text: The 天依 slope in 酒泉. Formed from 𨸏, with 衣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9627.text: 陝 in 弘農, the ancient state of Guo, where King Ji's son was enfeoffed. Formed from 𨸏, with 夾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9628.text: The eastern corner of 陝, 弘農. Formed from 𨸏, with 無 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9629.text: A corner of 安邑, 河東. Formed from 𨸏, with 卷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9630.text: The 陭氏 slope in 上黨. Formed from 𨸏, with 奇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9631.text: The western pass of the northern hills: 雁門. Formed from 𨸏, with 俞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9632.text: The 五阮 pass in 代 commandery. Formed from 𨸏, with 元 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9633.text: A great hill. Alternatively, there is a 䧊 hill in 𨞅, 右扶風. Formed from 𨸏, with 告 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9634.text: A hill's name. Formed from 𨸏, with 武 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9635.text: A hill's name. Formed from 𨸏, with 貞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9636.text: A hill's name. Formed from 𨸏, with 丁 indicating the sound. Read like 丁.

shuowen:9637.text: A slope in Zheng territory. Formed from 𨸏, with 爲 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: 'They would meet the earl of Zheng at 䧦.'

shuowen:9638.text: An islet-like hill is 陼丘: high ground in water. Formed from 𨸏, with 者 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9639.text: 宛丘, where Gui Man, descendant of Shun, was enfeoffed. Formed from 𨸏 and 木, with 申 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9640.text: A hill with two tiers, in 濟陰. Formed from 𨸏, with 匋 indicating the sound. The Book of Xia says: 'Eastward to Tao Hill.' Tao Hill has Yao's city, where Yao once lived; hence Yao's title Taotang.

shuowen:9641.text: In tilling, to dig with a spade and bring out the hard soil below. Alternatively, to plow fallow land. Formed from 𨸏 and 土, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9642.text: A wall being precarious. Formed from 𨸏, with 占 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9643.text: The steps of a hall. Formed from 𨸏, with 余 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9644.text: Steps. Formed from 𨸏, with 皆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9645.text: The host's staircase. Formed from 𨸏, with 乍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9646.text: Steps for ascending high. Formed from 𨸏, with 坒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9647.text: The succession of steps. Formed from 𨸏, with 亥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9648.text: The meeting of walls. Formed from 𨸏, with 祭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9649.text: An opening at a wall's joint. Formed from 𨸏 and 𡭴; 𡭴 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:9650.text: Piled earth. Alternatively, full. Formed from 𨸏, with 咅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9651.text: A low wall beside a road. Formed from 𨸏, with 彖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9652.text: The sound of building a wall. Formed from 𨸏, with 耎 indicating the sound. The Odes says: 'They fill it, resounding.'

shuowen:9653.text: The parapet atop a city wall. Formed from 𨸏, with 卑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9654.text: A city's moat: with water it is 池; without water, 隍. Formed from 𨸏, with 皇 indicating the sound. The Changes says: 'The wall returns to the moat.'

shuowen:9655.text: A cattle or horse enclosure formed along a mountain valley. Formed from 𨸏, with 去 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9656.text: Precarious. Formed from 𨸏, with 垂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9657.text: A small barrier. Alternatively, a low city wall. Formed from 𨸏, with 烏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9658.text: Firm. Formed from 𨸏, with 完 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9659.text: A hollow in a mountain or hill. Formed from 𨸏, with 侖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9660.text: A hill by water. Formed from 𨸏, with 辰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9661.text: A hill by water. Formed from 𨸏, with 戔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9662.text: A hill's name. Formed from 𨸏, with 卂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9663.text: An east-west road is 陌; a north-south road is 阡. Formed from 𨸏, with 千 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9664.text: The space between two hills. Formed from two 𨸏. All characters in this group are formed from 𨺅.

shuowen:9665.text: An opening in a hill. Formed from 𨺅, with abbreviated 決 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9666.text: Cramped and narrow, as in 𨹟. Formed from 𨺅, with 纷 indicating the sound. 纷 is the large-seal character 嗌, according to the recorded component notation.

shuowen:9667.text: One who guards beacon fires at a frontier watch-post. Formed from 𨺅 and 火, with 遂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9668.text: To heap dug earth into walls. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 厽.

shuowen:9669.text: To increase. Formed from 厽 and 糸. A 絫 is the weight of ten millet grains.

shuowen:9670.text: To pile up unfired bricks. Formed from 厽 and 土.

shuowen:9671.text: A yin number. It depicts division into four. All characters in this group are formed from 四.

shuowen:9672.text: To sort and accumulate things. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 宁.

shuowen:9673.text: A 㡒 container, used to carry and hold rice. Formed from 宁 and 甾. 甾 is a jar.

shuowen:9674.text: To connect in succession. A pictograph. All characters in this group are formed from 叕.

shuowen:9675.text: To join and attach. Formed from 叕 and 糸.

shuowen:9676.text: Ugly. It depicts a person with a hunched back. Attendant Jia says it means rank or sequence. All characters in this group are formed from 亞.

shuowen:9678.text: The five phases. Formed from 二, with yin and yang crossing between heaven and earth. All characters in this group are formed from 五.

shuowen:9679.text: A number of the Changes: yin changes at six and is regular at eight. Formed from 入 and 八. All characters in this group are formed from 六.

shuowen:9680.text: The regular number of yang. Formed from 一, with faint yin emerging obliquely from the middle. All characters in this group are formed from 七.

shuowen:9681.text: The changing number of yang. It depicts its curving to ultimate completion. All characters in this group are formed from 九.

shuowen:9682.text: A road accessible in nine directions. Resembling a turtle's back, it is therefore called 馗. 馗 means high. Formed from 九 and 首.

shuowen:9683.text: A beast's feet trampling the earth. A pictograph, with 九 indicating the sound. The Erya says: 'Foxes, badgers, and raccoon dogs have 𨆌 feet and 厹 tracks.' All characters in the 厹 group are formed from 厹.

shuowen:9684.text: A general name for running beasts. Formed from 厹; a pictograph, with 今 indicating the sound. The heads of 禽, 离, and 兕 resemble one another.

shuowen:9685.text: A mountain spirit, a beast. Formed from the head of 禽, with 厹 and 屮. Ouyang Qiao says 离 is a fierce beast.

shuowen:9686.text: A creature. Formed from 厹; a pictograph.

shuowen:9687.text: A creature. Formed from 厹; a pictograph.

shuowen:9688.text: In King Cheng of Zhou's time, the state of 州靡 presented a 𥝋: human-bodied, with reversed heels, laughing by itself; when it laughs, its upper lip covers its eyes. It eats people. In the north it is called 土螻. The Erya says: '𥝋𥝋 resembles a person with loose hair.' Also named 䲷陽. Formed from 厹; a pictograph.

shuowen:9689.text: A creature. Formed from 厹; a pictograph. Pronounced the same as 偰.

shuowen:9690.text: Livestock, as in 㹌. It depicts ears, head, and feet treading the ground. Ancient-script 嘼 has 厹 below. All characters in this group are formed from 嘼.

shuowen:9691.text: That which guards and keeps watch. Formed from 嘼 and 犬.

shuowen:9692.text: The first of the eastern series, when yang vital energy begins to sprout and stir. It depicts 木, wood, wearing 孚甲, a seed casing. Alternatively, the human head should be 甲, and 甲 depicts a head. All characters in this group are formed from 甲.

shuowen:9693.text: It depicts spring plants emerging bent and twisting: yin vital energy is still strong, so they emerge crookedly. The same conception as 丨. 乙 follows 甲 and depicts a person's neck. All characters in this group are formed from 乙.

shuowen:9694.text: To emerge upward. Formed from 乙, representing things coming through, with 倝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9695.text: To put in order. Formed from 乙, which orders it, and 𤔔.

shuowen:9696.text: Different or unusual. Formed from 乙, with 又 indicating the sound.

shuowen:9697.text: Its position is in the south, where all things mature and shine brightly. Yin vital energy first arises; yang is about to decline. Formed from 一 entering 冂. 一 is yang. 丙 follows 乙 and depicts a person's shoulders. All characters in this group are formed from 丙.

shuowen:9698.text: In summer, all things become firm and substantial. A pictograph. 丁 follows 丙 and depicts a person's heart. All characters in this group are formed from 丁.

shuowen:9699.text: The central palace. It depicts the six 甲 and five dragons entwined and gripping one another. 戊 follows 丁 and depicts a person's ribs. All characters in this group are formed from 戊.

shuowen:9700.text: To accomplish. Formed from 戊, with 丁 indicating the sound.
